raw_response:
I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize cycle, because that is what pays steady here and I have well water, so I can push yield without gambling too much. I do not start from zero every year. I look at what worked last year, what the neighbors with clean fields and full grain carts did, and then I adjust a little. On my 12 mu, I will keep 10 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same ground, and I will leave 2 mu for cotton. With fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than watch the crop go yellow at jointing or filling time. But I still count money closely, because if I overspend on fertilizer, then I feel it later when I need pesticide, diesel, or hired help. For wheat here, I will use improved seed, put most phosphorus down as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, and give 3 irrigations if the season is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, go a little heavier on nitrogen, and keep 2 irrigations ready because summer rain cannot be trusted. For cotton, I will keep only a small area, use hybrid seed, give more potassium than wheat or maize, and spray more times because cotton is more troublesome and I do not want insects to eat the profit.
